newsitem.title: MEXICO: United Airlines plans more code-shares.
newsitem.headline: United Airlines plans more code-shares.

text.p: United Airlines plans to complete further code-sharing agreements within the coming months, company vice president Chris Bowers told reporters in a recent visit here following a code-sharing alliance with airline Mexicana de Aviacion.

"We have a few others we are talking to, but that's all I'm going to say right now," Bowers said. "We believe that the partnerships that we wish to work with, that share the same vision we do, will all be done in the next few months."

"We will expand when we can do so and make money," he said, of United's presence in Latin America. United is the largest U.S. carrier in Mexico, according to Bowers and Latin America is the company's third largest revenue-producing region outside the United States.
Signing the code-sharing alliance with one of Mexico's two largest airlines, the United vice president signaled such partnerships are crucial for regional competitiveness.
"We do not believe any carrier anymore can go it alone and serve the customer base on a global reach. You simply can't do it, you've got to have alliances," he said.

British Airways and American Airlines earlier this month decided to join forces, sharing travel destinations in a surprise move for two airlines that had preferred to go solo. The code-share agreement awaits regulatory approval.
"If American and British Airways get together, that's fine. Competition is good," Bowers said.
United is a division of Chicago-based UAL Corp., and Mexicana is a unit of Mexican airline holding company Cintra.
